summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Stratagem Cloud. Stratagem is a GPU-focused cloud provider targeting mid-market AI customers across EMEA and NA, interested in partnership for offering Redwood Dedicated and hosting Redwood-managed inference for their customers. Key themes: compatibility/validation for GPUs (A100/H100 equivalents), networking (VPC connectivity, private link), commercial incentives for co-selling, and a technical pilot to validate performance and routing. Action items and schedule for a technical deep-dive and benchmarks were agreed.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Tom Garcia (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Stratagem CTO), Priya Reddy (Head of Cloud Partnerships), Daniel Morales (Infra Lead), Sofia Alvarez (Biz Dev)
---
[00:00] Tom: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Tom from Redwood, im the partner lead, with me are Sanjay and Maya from our engineering team. how are you all?
[00:12] Alex: good, thanks. excited to chat. quick note, we have Priya and Daniel on, they run most of the infra and partnerships.
[00:20] Priya: hi all, thanks for setting this up. we saw the partnership deck, interested in exploring deeper.
[00:28] Tom: great, i'll do a quick 5 minute partner program overview then pass to sanjay for technical fit and then we can talk commercial models. sound OK?
[00:37] Priya: yep sounds good.
[00:40] Tom: quick overview: Redwood does hosted inference, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. partner program includes co-sell, joint go-to-market, and a technical partner tier where we validate compatibility and publish perf profiles. typical partner flow is validation -> pilot -> launch.
[00:58] Alex: can you clarify dedicated vs private? what would run in our cloud versus Redwood-managed?
[01:06] Tom: sure. dedicated is reserved capacity that we can run on your fleet or in a dedicated cluster we manage; private is a customer-managed private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where our control plane is segregated. for partners we often do a managed dedicated offering hosted on partner infra with mixed responsibilities.
[01:25] Daniel: when you say control plane, do you require outbound connectivity to Redwood? any air-gapped options?
[01:32] Sanjay: good question, currently the default flow expects a control plane connection for telemetry and rollouts, but we have options for private deployments with limited outbound and we can discuss air-gap packaging; it'll affect upgrade cadence.
[01:47] Maya: also worth mentioning KMS/HSM integration for key management, and audit logs for compliance.
[01:54] Alex: that helps. our main focus is latency for EU customers, and cost predictability. we run a mix of H100-class and A100-class instances, some custom SKUs.
[02:04] Sanjay: perfect. do you have rough numbers for GPU counts and regions?
[02:09] Alex: roughly 120 H100-ish GPUs across EU-west and 60 in NA, plus some A100s for older customers. we'll share a spreadsheet.
[02:18] Tom: great. on the commercial side we typically do a revenue share for managed deployments or wholesale capacity pricing for dedicated. co-sell incentives vary by tier.
[02:27] Sofia: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[02:30] Tom: usually 4-8 weeks for a scoped benchmark pilot. if partner infra is compatible we can accelerate.
[02:36] Priya: ok, can you talk to us about networking -- private link, VPC peering, throughput for KV cache use?
[02:44] Sanjay: for low-latency setups we recommend colocated subnets and private connectivity. we support VPC peering and private link equivalents; for KV cache and model weights we have options to keep traffic within the partner network. there will be some firewall rules and ports to open; we'll send a technical checklist.
[03:03] Daniel: latency budget: we're seeing customer SLAs of sub-150ms for small chat workloads. can you meet that on H100-class?
[03:10] Sanjay: depends on model and quantization; for optimized models and lower sequence lengths we can hit 50-120ms on H100 variants in many cases. we'll need to test with your images and kernel builds.
[03:22] Alex: do you require specific CUDA/cuDNN versions? we have several clusters with different drivers.
[03:29] Maya: we publish a compatibility matrix but we can run validations; some older drivers cause perf regressions for certain ops. we'll want to run a quick validation across your fleet.
[03:41] Tom: want to talk about billing and pricing briefly -- partners often ask about unit economics and committed vs burst capacity.
[03:48] Alex: yes, economics are the main value prop for customers choosing stratagem; how would Redwood affect our margins?
[03:55] Tom: for managed dedicated we can do wholesale pricing with a commit; we also provide recommendations via Redwood Optimize to help reduce per-token cost with batching and quantization profiles. we can share anonymized benchmarks.
[04:07] Priya: security controls: we need SOC2 and audit log capabilities, SSO for account management, and RBAC.
[04:15] Maya: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC and long-term audit retention as an add-on. we'll include our security pack docs.
[04:25] Daniel: on networking again, if we host the model weights locally, is there a fallback path to Redwood hosted models?
[04:32] Sanjay: yes, routing policies can fallback to a hosted variant. that said, fallback may have latencies and data residency implications. we can set policies per route.
[04:44] Alex: curious about model variants and quantization - do you support int8, nf4, etc?
[04:50] Sanjay: we support a range of quantization formats depending on architecture and kernel availability; Redwood Optimize recommends per-workload options.
[04:58] Sofia: what about shared customers and co-selling? what commitments do you expect?
[05:03] Tom: typically joint GTM playbooks, referral credits for early deals, and lead sharing. tiered benefits come with technical validation and minimum sales targets for co-sell. flexible to negotiate.
[05:15] Alex: great. can we scope a pilot: basic perf benchmark using a 13B open model + a typical chat prompt set, run across 10 H100 nodes in EU-west for 72 hours?
[05:27] Sanjay: yes that's straightforward. we'd like to run A/B: your current stack vs Redwood runtime, measure latency, throughput, token costs, and failure modes.
[05:36] Maya: we'll need access to your container images or allow us to run our runtime on a test partition; what do you prefer?
[05:42] Daniel: prefer we run Redwood on our images initially to ensure kernel compatibility, then maybe let Redwood run their managed stack.
[05:49] Sanjay: that works. we'll document both flows in the test plan.
[05:53] Tom: ok next steps recap: Tom to send partner one-pager and partner terms; Sanjay to draft a benchmark plan; Alex to share inventory and network diagrams. we should have a tech deep-dive in two weeks.
[06:06] Alex: agreed. one question: are there any exclusivity or lock-in clauses in your partner terms?
[06:12] Tom: no hard exclusivity; partnership can be non-exclusive. we try to be flexible.
[06:18] Priya: what about support SLAs for managed deployments?
[06:22] Maya: Dedicated has optional SLA tiers; we can map those to support response times.
[06:27] Sofia: any red flags for compliance when we run customer data through Redwood?
[06:31] Maya: with private deployments and customer-managed control plane we can limit data exfiltration. we'll share the security whitepaper and DSGs.
[06:40] Tom: okay, anything else?
[06:42] Daniel: one minor, our billing systems expect monthly invoicing. is that supported?
[06:47] Tom: yes monthly invoicing is common for partners.
[06:50] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the inventory and schedule.
[06:54] Tom: thanks all. we'll send the deck and schedule the deep-dive.
---
